title: Rejection hides odd mask biases to second order: key recovery needs eps^-4 signatures for a linear y tilt, eps^-2 for an even bias
claim: If the mask y has density proportional to 1 + eps*f(y/gamma1) instead of uniform, the accepted z = y + c s1 has conditional mean E[z_j | u_j] = a + g*u_j with u = c s1, and least squares of z on rot(c) recovers s1 from N* = 16 sigma_z^2 / (tau g^2) signatures. For an ODD defect f(x) = x the gain is second order, g = eps^2 B^2/(3 G^2), so N* scales as eps^-4; for an EVEN defect f(x) = x^2 it is first order, g = -2 eps B^2/(3 G^2), so N* scales as eps^-2 (G = gamma1, B = gamma1 - beta). At toyDSA(32,2,2) with gamma1 = 2^6 the two fitted slopes are -4 and -2 within +-0.5, and eps = 0 gives no recovery.
mechanism: Rejection sampling hides u only because the accepted density of z, p(z - u) restricted to the box, is flat. For a perturbed density the u-dependence of the accepted mean comes from the perturbation's derivative inside the box: an even perturbation (curvature, as produced by summed or edge-biased samplers) has a z-linear cross term -2 eps u z / G^2 at first order, while an odd linear tilt moves the mean only through the normalising constant 1 - eps u / G, a second-order effect. So the parity of a sampler defect, not its size, sets the exponent of the signature count, which is the quantity a defect triage needs and which the uniform-y proof does not discuss.

title: One signature gives s1 mod 2^b from an exact b-bit LSB leak of y: c is a unit mod 2^b iff tau is odd (ML-DSA-44/65, not 87)
claim: If the low b bits of every mask coefficient y_j leak (for example from a table-indexed ExpandMask unpack), then z - y_low = 2^b y_high + c s1 gives c s1 mod 2^b exactly, and since c(1), the sum of tau signs, is congruent to tau mod 2, c is invertible in Z_{2^b}[X]/(X^n+1) whenever tau is odd (39 and 49 at ML-DSA-44/65), so ONE signature yields s1 mod 2^b; at b >= ceil(log2(2 eta + 1)) that is s1 itself. At ML-DSA-87 (tau = 60) c is never a unit mod 2 and one signature leaves a kernel. With with partial leakage (a fraction rho of coefficients) the remaining unknowns are finished with DDGR modular hints plus BKZ.
mechanism: X^n + 1 = (X + 1)^n mod 2, so an element of Z_2[X]/(X^n+1) is a unit iff its value at X = 1 is odd, and Hensel lifting extends units to Z_{2^b}. c in B_tau has c(1) congruent to tau mod 2; tau = 39, 49, 60 at ML-DSA-44/65/87, so ML-DSA-87's c is NOT invertible mod 2 and needs a different finish (prediction P3). The z-bound rejection does not alter z = y + c s1 for accepted signatures, so the leak is exact through rejection. Partial leakage turns each known LSB into a modular hint on one linear form of s1, and DDGR's modular-hint integration predicts the remaining block size.

title: Hedged entropy is load-bearing only if rho'' drops K or mu: signatures-to-s1 vs rnd entropy h for three derivations
claim: With the FIPS 204 derivation rho'' = H(K || rnd || mu), signatures-to-key-recovery is infinite at every rnd entropy h from 0 to 256 bits: degraded rnd costs nothing against a passive observer. If K is dropped (rho'' = H(rnd || mu)), one signature plus 2^h ExpandMask evaluations recovers s1; if mu is dropped (rho'' = H(K || rnd)), a mask collision between different messages appears after about 2^{h/2} signatures and one colliding pair gives s1 = (c1 - c2)^{-1}(z1 - z2). Both defective arms verify under a conformant verifier.
mechanism: y = ExpandMask(rho'', kappa) is fully determined by rho''. With K inside, an observer cannot evaluate y even when rnd is known; with mu inside, equal rnd on different messages gives unrelated masks. Dropping K makes y a public function of a low-entropy rnd and a known message, so z - y = c s1 and c is invertible mod q with overwhelming probability. Dropping mu makes y depend only on (K, rnd), so equal rnd across messages reuses y with kappa equal whenever both signatures accept on the same iteration, and z1 - z2 = (c1 - c2) s1 exactly. This turns the RQ's hedged-vs-deterministic question into three measured curves.
tracked_object: number of signatures and ExpandMask work until exact s1 recovery, as a function of rnd entropy h, for three rho'' derivations

title: Leaked aborted FSwA transcripts: edge inequalities on rejected z recover s1 far faster than ILWE regression on the same leak
claim: If an implementation exposes rejected attempts (z_rej, c_rej) (debug logs, a retry API, or an unprotected loop), each coordinate with |z_j| >= gamma1 - beta gives an inequality on (c s1)_j with threshold uniform in [-beta, beta]. An inequality-constrained solver (linear programming plus BKZ finish) recovers s1 at toyDSA(64,2,2) from at least 30 times fewer rejected attempts than least-squares ILWE regression on the same leaked z, whose requirement is about 16 gamma1^2 / (3 tau).
mechanism: A rejected z is y + c s1 with uniform y and no truncation, so its mean carries s1 only with noise variance gamma1^2/3, which is ILWE with huge noise. But z_j lies in [-gamma1 + 1 + u_j, gamma1 + u_j], so coordinates near the edge pin u_j = (c s1)_j from one side with resolution about gamma1 - |z_j|; extreme values give inequalities of width O(beta), roughly 2^10 times tighter information per useful coordinate than the mean. Accumulating thousands of such half-space constraints over the s1 box shrinks the feasible set to one point; the inequality-hint integration of LWE side-information work then finishes.

title: Hash arm made measurable: forge at real ML-DSA-44 against defective SampleInBall images of 2^16..2^32 and test cost = |image|

title: Masking order as a measured security parameter for c*s1: traces-to-key vs SNR at order d = 0, 1, 2 in a simulated Hamming-weight model
claim: In a simulated Hamming-weight leakage of the product c*s1 computed coefficient-wise in the NTT domain with d+1 arithmetic shares and Gaussian noise sigma, the number of signatures needed to recover s1 by correlation/template attack with known c grows as sigma^{2(d+1)} at fixed d. title: A defective ExpandA zeroing NTT slots of A leaks s2 in those slots from pk alone: block size vs number of bad slots

title: Naive threshold ML-DSA leaks through the mask sum: an Irwin-Hall shaped y makes post-rejection z regress on c s1 with gain near 1
claim: A naive T-party threshold signer that sums per-party uniform masks y = sum y_i and applies the FIPS rejection bound produces accepted z whose conditional mean is E[z_j | u_j] = g_T * u_j with g_T >= 0.8 for T >= 3, so least-squares on public signatures recovers s1 with about 16 sigma_z^2/(tau g_T^2) signatures. At toyDSA(64,2,2) with gamma1 = 2^10 this is predicted at about 1.4*10^5 signatures for T = 4 with per-party range gamma1/T, while T = 1 (uniform) shows no recovery at 10^6.
mechanism: Rejection sampling hides u only if the mask density is flat over the acceptance window; a sum of T uniforms is piecewise polynomial with density falling toward the box edge, so truncating y + u to the box barely changes the mean shift u. The gain g_T = 1 - 2B p_T(B)/P_T(|Y| < B) approaches 1 as the density at the edge vanishes. Threshold designs that rescale per-party ranges or use boundary-clearance techniques exist precisely to avoid this; measuring the naive leak quantifies what they protect.

title: Hedging priced against faults: differential recovery needs 2^{h/2} same-message queries with h-bit rnd; census of mode-independent faults
claim: For single-bit faults on c (or on mu before the challenge hash), differential recovery z - z' = (c - c') s1 needs two signatures of the same message with the same mask. In deterministic mode this needs 2 signing queries; with an rnd source of h bits it needs about 2^{h/2} same-message queries; with caller-supplied rnd (an API exposing it) it collapses to 2. Measured on real ML-DSA-44 with simulated faults, median queries to recovery fit 2^{h/2} within factor 2 for h in {8..24}, and a census of fault positions shows which positions are mode-independent (attack works in hedged mode at h = 256).
mechanism: rho'' = H(K || rnd || mu): equal masks need equal (rnd, mu). A fault after rho'' (e.g. on c) with the mask reused gives an exact linear relation. Hedging thus converts a 2-query attack into a birthday search over rnd. Faults that do not need mask reuse (e.g. zeroing y, skipping the addition) are unaffected by hedging; the census separates the two classes, which is a mode-dependent fault boundary.

title: Repudiable keys by rho grinding: cost law q^{k-l+1}/256 for a rank-deficient NTT slot of A, and its honest frequency
claim: The probability that a uniformly expanded k x l slot matrix over F_q is rank-deficient is about q^{-(k-l+1)}; at true q = 8380417 and k = l = 4 that is 2^-23 per slot, 2^-15 per key over 256 slots. A key owner grinding rho finds a key with a rank-deficient slot in about 2^15 ExpandA calls at ML-DSA-44 shape (k = l), and whether such keys give any forgery advantage is tested rather than assumed. Measured median grind cost within factor 2 of 1/(256 q^{-(k-l+1)}), and the honest-key rate of degenerate slots matches the same law.
mechanism: For k = l (ML-DSA-44), square slot matrices are singular with probability about 1/q, so over 256 slots and modest grinding, singular slots are common enough to appear in honest keys too (about 2^-15 per key). A verifier cannot cheaply know whether the owner chose rho to create this. Whether a singular slot gives a usable advantage is tested by the forger measuring success of slot-local SIS against such keys vs honest ones.
tracked_object: grind cost to a singular slot, honest-key singular-slot frequency, and forgery advantage

binomial CI covers prediction over 2^20 keys

title: Masked signers vs the exact signing-only predicates: boundary-forced differential testing of masked vs reference rejections
claim: Masked ML-DSA implementations evaluate ||z||_inf < gamma1 - beta, the LowBits bound and the hint-weight gate on shares via A2B conversions; an off-by-one or carry bug changes the rejection set without affecting verification of accepted signatures for the self-enforcing z check, but for the signing-only ct0/hint gates it is invisible to verify. Forcing y (via test hooks) to land within +-2 of each boundary, a masked implementation's decisions match the unmasked reference on 10^7 forced cases, or the first mismatch is exhibited; a planted carry bug is detected within 10^4 forced cases.
mechanism: Random testing never reaches the signing-only boundaries (rates below 10^-9); boundary forcing by choosing y or c makes each predicate's edge reachable directly, and comparing decision bits between masked and unmasked code isolates masking-induced errors.

title: The integrity dual of t0 secrecy: how many low bit-planes of t0 in the secret key can be corrupted before signatures stop verifying
claim: If the low b bit-planes of the signer's stored t0 are randomised, the hint is computed from c t0' instead of c t0 and a signature fails verification only when the error c e pushes a coefficient across a HighBits boundary. Predicted per-signature failure rate is n k sqrt(2/pi) sqrt(tau/6) 2^b / (2 gamma2) for small b: about 2 percent at b = 1 and 17 percent at b = 4 at ML-DSA-44, about 11 percent at b = 4 at ML-DSA-65; the fit holds within factor 2 for b in {1..5} and saturates above. So low-plane t0 integrity faults are largely silent to verification, the dual of how little t0 a public observer needs.
mechanism: t0 enters signing only through c t0 in the hint; a randomised low-plane error e has variance about 2^{2b}/6, so c e has standard deviation sqrt(tau/6) 2^b, and a coefficient fails only if it lies within |c e| of a HighBits boundary, probability |c e|/(2 gamma2). The rate quantifies how much of t0 the signer actually uses, the dual of how much of t0 a public observer learns.
tracked_object: verify-failure rate vs number of corrupted t0 bit-planes
